newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed higher at 8.2928 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Friday due to a technical rebound after a sharp fall on Thursday saw the yuan end at a one-month low of 8.2941, traders said.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2921.
Dealers said bargain-hunting emerged on Friday after the yuan closed sharply lower on Thursday due to intervention by the central bank, the People's Bank.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2941 and moved in a wide range in early trading, hitting an intraday high of 8.2920 and a low of 8.2952. It then stabilised to move mainly around 8.2930.
Trading was active in early trading but dull for the rest of the session with most business done at 8.2932, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan was under-valued after Thursday's fall.
"Buying at the low level set in immediately after the opening, which pushed the yuan to the higher close," he said.
A second dealer said Friday's rebound was weak with the market fearing further intervention by the central bank to depress the yuan.
"The central bank's action on Thursday has made traders cautious," he said.
Dealers said they expected the yuan to move in a range of 8.2920 and 8.2930 early next week.
The yuan closed down at 7.1465 from 7.1355 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0700 from 1.0702 against the Hong Kong dollar.
